what_happened: After handoff the ego braked hard on an open highway, from 23.7 to 6.3 m/s, though the nearest lead was more than 40 m ahead. That let actor 1, a replayed car in the next lane to the left, catch up and pull alongside. The ego's path then wobbled left, about 1.4 m off the recorded trajectory, and its front-left corner clipped actor 1 as it passed. A rear contact was also recorded, but this front collision is the at-fault failure.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command (it switched to RIGHT at the end), the ego slowed from 6.7 to 4.5 m/s. Its planned path bent left, away from the recorded path, and the ego drifted into the left lane. Its front hit actor 41, a white pickup that was passing on the left.

Its planned path (the orange line) bent left and the ego drifted left out of its lane on the highway, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. It hit the white pickup (actor 41) in the adjacent left lane with its front at about 4.6 m/s, about 1.5 m off the recorded human path.

On an open highway (command STRAIGHT, then RIGHT), the ego braked hard for no visible reason, from 24 to 7.7 m/s, with no lead vehicle within about 42 m, and drifted slightly left. Log-replayed car 1, coming up from behind in the left lane, made side contact with it at 7.1 s (the run is also flagged rear-ended). The policy's unneeded hard braking and drift, not another actor, set up the crash.

On a clear multi-lane highway with no lead vehicle close (gap over 40 m), the ego braked hard for no visible reason, slowing from 24 to 7.5 m/s. While braking, it drifted about 1.2 m left toward the lane line, into the path of actor 1, which was coming up from behind in the left lane, and the two sideswiped (a lateral collision, followed by rear contact).

After handoff on an open highway, the ego braked hard for no visible reason (23.7 to 6.4 m/s with no lead closer than about 44 m), and it drifted left across its lane line. Actor 1, overtaking in the left-adjacent lane, came alongside and ahead, and the ego's front-left corner struck it. The rear contact came from traffic behind running into the sharply decelerating ego.

The ego was on a wet multi-lane freeway with a RIGHT route command and slowing from about 6.7 to 4.4 m/s. Its planned path bent left, and it drifted across the left lane line, about 1.5 m off the recorded trajectory. Its front-left corner hit actor 41, a white SUV passing in the adjacent left lane.

On a multi-lane highway with the route going straight, then right, the ego's planned path kept veering left. At 7.7 s it steered into the adjacent left lane and hit actor 41, a white SUV driving alongside, with its front corner while the recorded human path continued straight and slightly right.

After slowing behind car 48, the ego's plan bent left (even though the route command was RIGHT), and the ego drifted over the left lane line. At 8.2 s it sideswiped car 7, which was driving alongside in the left lane. The earlier front-collision flag is not counted: the per-timestep front value is zero in all three frames shown, so that contact most likely happened before handoff at 4.7 s.

The ego was slowing behind actor 48 on the highway, then turned left out of its lane and away from the recorded path (the command was STRAIGHT, then RIGHT) into the next lane, where actor 7 was coming up beside it. At 8.2 s the ego's side hit actor 7 while the ego was about 2 m off the recorded path and drifting left.

After the policy took over at 4.7s, the ego braked hard and stayed close behind slow lead car 48 (gap 3.8–6.4 m). It then steered left toward the adjacent lane, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, and at 8.2s its left side hit actor 7, which was driving alongside in that lane (lateral collision).

On the highway at about 5–6 m/s, the ego's heading drifted left across the lane markings, even though the route command changed to RIGHT. It sideswiped actor 7, which was travelling alongside in the adjacent left lane just behind the ego. The lead car was 35 m ahead and did not matter, and the side contact happened about 1.8 m off the recorded human path.

After nearly closing on lead car 48 around 5–6 s, the ego slowed and then steered left off its route, even though the command was RIGHT. At 8.2 s it was crossing into the adjacent left lane and sideswiped actor 7, which was coming up alongside in that lane; the metrics log this as a lateral collision.

On a multi-lane freeway with a RIGHT command, the ego drove slowly (3–4.6 m/s), fell about 10 m behind its recorded position, and drifted about 1.8 m left of the recorded path toward the left lane line. At 8.7 s its left side hit vehicle 7, which was coming up alongside in the adjacent left lane.

The ego slowed behind lead car 48 in stop-and-go freeway traffic and then drifted left toward the adjacent lane, even though the route command was RIGHT. Car 7 was coming up from behind in that left lane, and at 8.2 s the two collided side-to-side, with the ego about 1.8 m off the recorded human path.

The ego was creeping along at 3–5 m/s in heavy freeway traffic and had drifted about 1.8 m left of the recorded human path, toward the lane on its left. Actor 7 was moving faster in that left lane, came up from behind and clipped the ego's left side at 8.7 s (lateral collision).

After slowing behind actor 48 in its lane, the ego steered left away from its route, even though the command was RIGHT. It drifted about 1.9 m off the recorded path toward the adjacent left lane, and actor 7 was coming up alongside in that lane. The ego's left side made contact with actor 7 at 8.7 s, which was flagged as a lateral collision.

After slowing behind actor 48, the ego drifted left toward the adjacent lane, even though the command was RIGHT, and ended up 1.9 m off the recorded path. At 8.2 s it side-swiped actor 7, which was coming up from behind on its left (a lateral collision).

On a straight highway segment at about 5.5–5.9 m/s, the ego drifted left of its lane center and yawed left, so its left side touched actor 7, which was driving next to it in the left lane slightly behind. The contact was lateral (collision_lateral=1 at 12.2s). The lead car stayed 17–35 m ahead throughout, so following distance played no part.

The ego was creeping along at 3–4.5 m/s behind slow traffic (actor 48), about 1.8 m to the left of the recorded human path and sitting on the left lane line. Actor 7, a replayed vehicle coming up from behind in the left lane, sideswiped the ego's left rear side at 8.2 s (a lateral collision). The ego didn't steer into it, but its leftward offset from the recording put it in the replayed car's path.
